WHY: previously the organization `slug` was written only when team billing was disabled; now it is written exactly when team billing is enabled, so organizations are created with a real slug before payment (while `requestedSlug` is also set), breaking the billing-gated slug flow. HOW: restore `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {} : { slug })`.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.texto:
WHAT: The new member routes `delete "members"` / `put "members"` inside `resources :groups` expose the group id under `:id`, but the target actions read `params.require(:group_id)`.
WHY: Bare routes inside a `resources` block are member routes, so the path is `/admin/groups/:id/members` (param `:id`), while `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`/`#remove_member` (groups_controller.rb:66, :85) do `params.require(:group_id)`. `:group_id` is never supplied, so every real `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/<id>/members.json` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400 — the add/remove-member feature is broken. The specs pass `group_id:` directly to xhr, bypassing routing, so they don't catch it.
HOW: Either change the routes to include the key, e.g. `delete ":group_id/members" => "groups#remove_member"` / `put ":group_id/members" => "groups#add_members"`, or make the controller read `params.require(:id)`.

WHAT: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members / limit 50 → 3 pages for only 2 real pages).
WHY: On the true last page `currentPage` (2) never equals `totalPages` (3), so `showingLast` stays false, the `next` action stays enabled, and clicking it sets `offset` to `user_count` and renders an empty page while the UI shows a non-existent page 3.
HOW: Use a ceiling division, e.g. `return Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"));`.

WHAT: remove_member passes a bare integer (`user_id`) to `group.users.delete(...)`, but `users` is a `has_many :through` collection whose `delete(*records)` expects associated record objects, not primary keys. WHY: unlike `destroy`, `delete` does not coerce numeric ids (see admin/users_controller.rb:128, which correctly passes `@user`), so this raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` and returns a 500 without removing the member (or, if unhandled by the association, deletes the wrong row). HOW: load the record first — `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))` — or reuse the existing model helper `group.remove(User.find(user_id))` (group.rb:276), which deletes the group_users join row.

fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.texto: WHAT: PasswordForm.configuredFor() now returns true for any user that has a passwordless passkey, even though the user has no password credential (the authenticator's own credential type). WHY: configuredFor is consumed outside re-authentication by DefaultAuthenticationFlow:445 (a REQUIRED, requiresUser authenticator that is not 'configured' is expected to raise CREDENTIAL_SETUP_REQUIRED/SETUP_REQUIRED) and by ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator:61 (conditional subflow 'user configured' evaluation). Adding isConditionalPasskeysEnabled here makes the password authenticator report itself as satisfied purely because passkeys are enabled for the realm and the user holds a passkey, so behavior changes for every login that reaches this form, not only the intended re-authentication case. HOW: only widen configuredFor when the execution is actually a re-authentication, e.g. gate the new clause on isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)/re-auth state, or move the passkey allowance into the re-auth-specific handling instead of the general configuredFor contract.

WHAT: the challenge(context, error, field) override now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) whenever isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and this override is also reached from the brute-force lockout path (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isDisabledByBruteForce -> challenge(context, disabledByBruteForceError(...), ...)). WHY: for PasswordForm context.getUser() is always non-null (requiresUser()==true), so previously (condition context.getUser()==null) the passkey conditional UI was never rendered on its error pages; now a temporarily/permanently brute-force-disabled account with a passkey gets the passkey conditional UI injected into the disabled-account page, and the passkey submission path (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.action -> WebAuthnAuthenticator.action) does not re-apply the brute-force check, so a locked-out account can be logged into via passkey, bypassing the lockout control. HOW: exclude the brute-force/disabled error paths from the conditional-UI fill (e.g. skip the fill when error is disabledByBruteForceError, or only fill for the normal invalid-credentials challenge).

frontend-asset-optimization-grafana-code.texto: WHAT: The exclusive write lock is acquired and held (via defer) across the blocking file read (os.Open + decode, line 60) and the CDN HTTP GET (readWebAssetsFromCDN, line 56), and the cache is not re-checked after the lock is acquired. WHY: Because the fast path only returns for cfg.Env != setting.Dev, every request in Dev mode takes the write lock and re-reads the manifest, serializing requests that previously ran concurrently and blocking all readers for the entire I/O duration; on cold start, N concurrent callers all recompute the manifest sequentially instead of one computing and the rest reusing the result. HOW: After acquiring the write lock, re-check entryPointAssetsCache (and cfg.Env) and return it if populated; and/or load the manifest outside the lock into a local value, then take the lock only to publish it (optionally with sync.Once for the non-Dev path) so network/file I/O is not performed while holding the exclusive lock.

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.texto: The new user-verification check indexes `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` without guarding for a missing 'sender' key. `build_integration` only adds 'sender' conditionally (`if state.get('sender')`, lines 376-377), and `installation.py:44` explicitly checks `if 'sender' not in integration.metadata`, confirming sender can be absent (e.g. an integration created through this pipeline, whose state carries only installation_id and github_authenticated_user). When sender is missing, `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended `github-integration-failed` error page. Use a guarded lookup, e.g. `integration.metadata.get('sender', {}).get('login')` and return `error(...)` when it is absent.

implement-access-token-context-encoding-.texto: The isAccessTokenId matcher never validates the grant shortcut, so the grant-type assertions in expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken are silently no-ops. The token id has the form session(2)+token(2)+grant(2)+":"+UUID (e.g. "onrtac:..."), so the grant occupies indices 4-5, but the code reads substring(3,5) which yields the token-type chars ("ta"), never the grant; additionally the branch is inverted — `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns "no match" when the grant DOES match. Net effect: only the "X:UUID" shape is checked, and the real invariant (correct grant shortcut per flow) is never verified; fixing only the indices would make every assertion fail because of the inverted comparison. Use substring(4,6) and return `true` (or fall through) when it equals expectedGrantShortcut, e.g. `if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

The constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. As written, a null rawTokenId is accepted, defeating the intent of the guard (and the error message is misleading). Change the argument to rawTokenId.

The decoder hardcodes a 6-character context split as 2/2/2, i.e. it requires the grant shortcut to be exactly 2 characters, but the newly added OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut javadoc states the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". A custom grant that follows the documented guidance (e.g. 3-char shortcut) makes encodeTokenId emit a 7-char context whose own access token id then throws IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6") on decode (used by introspection/userInfo paths). Either make the grant shortcut length contract explicit/enforced (validate getShortcut length == 2 at registration) or make the decoder derive the grant-shortcut segment length instead of assuming 2.

notification-rule-processing-engine-graf.texto: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` (line 245), dropping the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` check. As a result federated Mimir rule groups are no longer treated as immutable, so Update/Delete/Pause/DeletePermanently abilities flip from NotSupported to supported and the edit/delete menu items become visible for rules the ruler API rejects. Restore the federation check for the CombinedRule path (e.g. compute isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and thread it into the abilities computation) instead of assuming false.

The grafana branch of the rules map renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without a `key` prop (the previous <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key}> had one). React list elements require a unique key; omitting it produces a missing-key warning and lets React reuse DOM/state incorrectly when the filtered list changes. Add key={key} to the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

The new OR-combination logic in AlertRuleMenu (lines 83-100, changed) makes canDelete/canPause true when only promRule is present (list view, rulerRule undefined). However the menu render still gates Pause on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) (line 123) and Delete on rulerRule && (line 165). These gates are unchanged but now inconsistent with the new ability semantics. In the list view, canDelete=true but the Delete item is never rendered.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.texto:
WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{success, data}`), but this code assigns that whole object to `key` and persists it as the credential key, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the parsed credential fields.
WHY: The stored key becomes `{success:true, data:{...}}` instead of the credential; the next construction calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75), which requires top-level access_token/refresh_token/scope/token_type/expiry_date, so it throws and the Google Calendar integration is permanently broken for that user.
HOW: Use the parsed data, e.g. `const { data: key } = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` (matching how office365calendar/zoom consume `.data`).

WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary-key id where the helper's third parameter is the owning `userId`.
WHY: In credential-sharing mode `refreshOAuthTokens` sends `calcomUserId: userId` to the external sync endpoint, so the wrong id (a credential id, not a user id) is transmitted, and the sharing branch is selected based on credential-id truthiness rather than whether the credential belongs to a user.
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` (available on the CredentialPayload) instead of `credentialId`.

WHAT: In credential-sharing mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object, while the non-sharing path returns the caller-specific parsed result; callers that treat the return as parsed data silently get wrong values.
WHY: hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192 reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` from a Response (undefined → NaN expiry persisted), and zohocrm/lib:217 and zoho-bigin/lib:96 read `tokenInfo.data.error` (Response has no `.data` → TypeError crash) whenever CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set.
HOW: Parse the response before returning (e.g. `return await response.json();`) or document/type the sync return consistently and update the data-consuming callers (hubspot, zohocrm, zoho-bigin) to match.

WHAT: After fetching and persisting a new access token, the `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` (the pre-refresh value) rather than the just-obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.
WHY: The connection that this block refreshes for is authenticated with the stale/expired token it was supposed to replace, so the refresh has no effect on the returned connection and requests can fail with an expired session.
HOW: Use the refreshed token when building the connection, e.g. `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.texto: WHAT: The order($val) mixin writes the raw value into the legacy/-webkit/-moz box properties ('-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val; -moz-box-ordinal-group: $val;') which are 1-based (default 1), while CSS 'order' is 0-based (default 0). WHY: These legacy properties require '$val + 1'; emitting '$val' produces an off-by-one ordinal group in old WebKit/Firefox flexbox (e.g. for $val <= 1 the item's legacy ordering no longer matches the modern 'order' value, so layouts differ between modern and legacy browsers). HOW: emit '-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1;' (and '-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1;'), keeping '-ms-flex-order'/'order' as $val.

plugins-chore-renamed-instrumentation-mi.texto: WHAT: ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics call instrumentContext(ctx, endpoint, req.PluginContext) with no nil-request guard, while the sibling LoggerMiddleware explicitly guards `if req == nil` before touching the request. WHY: ContextualLoggerMiddleware is placed OUTSIDE LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares (pluginsintegration.go indices 2 vs 3, and lower index is the outer wrapper per clientFromMiddlewares/decorator.go:101-125), so on a nil request it dereferences req.PluginContext first and panics, making LoggerMiddleware's existing nil-guard unreachable — a regression of a previously handled case into a crash. HOW: mirror the LoggerMiddleware guard (e.g. `if req == nil { return m.next.QueryData(ctx, req) }`) in every ContextualLoggerMiddleware method before calling instrumentContext.

WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware captures a single shared *MetricsMiddleware (imw) and mutates imw.next = next inside the ClientMiddlewareFunc closure, which is re-invoked on every request by Decorator.clientFromMiddlewares. WHY: concurrent plugin requests write and read the same imw.next field without synchronization, a data race (the inner middlewares return new instances per call, so next differs between requests), and a request can end up invoking a chain built for another request. HOW: return a fresh instance per invocation like every other middleware in this package, e.g. newMetricsMiddleware needs to expose the metrics but the factory should construct a new MetricsMiddleware per call (register metrics once, then inside the closure return &MetricsMiddleware{pluginMetrics: ..., pluginRegistry: ..., next: next}).

ref-crons-reorganize-incident-creation-i.texto: WHAT: `get_monitor_environment_context` computes a transformed local `config` (replacing `schedule_type` with its human-readable display via `get_schedule_type_display()`), but the returned dict sets `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` — the raw, untransformed config — so the local `config` is discarded. WHY: the intended `schedule_type` display conversion never reaches the occurrence/event context, so the monitor context emitted to the issue platform shows the raw numeric schedule type instead of the display string; the transformed value is dead code and the output is wrong. HOW: return the local `config` variable (i.e. `"config": config`) so the computed `schedule_type` display substitution is actually used.

replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.texto:
WHAT: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature is enabled, the table branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — hardcoded empty columns and data — instead of the computed `tableResults`/`eventView` used by the fallback branch.
WHY: Any organization with the flag on sees a permanently empty dashboard table (no headers, no rows), silently discarding the real query results.
HOW: Map the actual `result.data`/`result.meta` and `fields`/`fieldAliases` into the `TableWidgetVisualization` props (or gate the new component behind the flag only once it is actually wired to the result).

WHAT: The `Visualize` class replaced `yAxes: readonly string[]` with a single `yAxis: string`, but `BaseVisualize`, `toJSON()` and several consumers still use `yAxes`; call sites such as `static/app/views/explore/savedQueries/exploreParams.tsx:29` (`visualizes.flatMap(v => v.yAxes)`), `.../components/queryTokens.tsx:48` (`visualization.yAxes.map(...)`) and `.../components/seerSearch.tsx:179` (`yAxes: v.yAxes`) read `yAxes` off visualize objects.
WHY: Wherever one of those consumers receives a `Visualize` instance rather than a raw `BaseVisualize`, `v.yAxes` is `undefined`, producing empty y-axes (dropped chart series) or a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')` crash.
HOW: Thread the new `yAxis` shape through every consumer (use `v.yAxis`), or keep `yAxes` as a derived getter returning `[this.yAxis]` so existing readers keep working.

When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature is enabled, the branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` with hardcoded empty data/columns instead of the actual `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, and `fieldAliases`. WHY: every dashboard table widget whose org has the flag enabled renders an empty table (headers and rows disappear), because the real query result is discarded. HOW: build `columns` from the real fields/result.meta and pass `tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}}` (and the field header map / custom renderer) to `TableWidgetVisualization` instead of the empty placeholders.

The `Visualize` class replaced `yAxes: readonly string[]` with `yAxis: string`, but the serialized contract and guards were not updated consistently: `BaseVisualize`/`toJSON()` still emit `{yAxes: [...]}` while `isVisualize` now checks `'yAxis' in value`, and `fromJSON` changed to return `Visualize[]`. WHY: values round-tripped through location/JSON are `BaseVisualize` objects (have `yAxes`, no `yAxis`), so any code path that obtains a serialize/deserialize result and reads `visualize.yAxis` (or feeds it back into `isVisualize`) gets `undefined`/false, producing empty chart axes or columns. HOW: keep the internal getter (`yAxis`) and the serialized shape (`yAxes`) strictly separated and make every reader/writer of aggregate fields go through one conversion helper, or add a `yAxis` getter/`yAxes` compatibility so both forms are always defined.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.texto: WHAT: The new `else` branch increments retryCount whenever `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value, but `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` (not an error) whenever SMS sending is locked for the user/team (`isLockedForSMSSending`, twilioProvider.ts:79-95). WHY: A temporary lock (user or any team membership with smsLockState LOCKED) is misclassified as a send failure; combined with the top `deleteMany({ OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] })`, the reminder is permanently deleted after two cron runs instead of being retried once the lock is lifted, silently dropping a valid reminder. HOW: only increment retryCount on a genuine send error (keep the increment in the catch block) and handle the locked/skipped return without counting it as a failure.

WHAT: The catch block now increments retryCount for every exception thrown anywhere in the loop body, including transient infrastructure errors (prisma.profile.findFirst, getBookerBaseUrl, the reminder lookups) that have nothing to do with SMS delivery. WHY: A transient DB/network hiccup will bump retryCount and, together with the `retryCount > 1` delete condition, permanently delete the reminder after two failed cron runs, whereas previously such an error was only logged and the reminder retried next run. HOW: scope the retry increment to SMS-provider failures (e.g. only increment around the scheduleSMS call) rather than the whole try/catch, so unrelated errors do not consume the retry budget.

The else branch in the SMS reminder scheduling logic increments retryCount when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value. Since scheduleSMS returns undefined when isLockedForSMSSending is true (twilioProvider.ts:92-95), this increment is code-backed and is covered by existing finding #1.
The catch block increments retryCount for any thrown error, including transient, rate-limit, and lock errors. This is covered by existing finding #2.

The deleteMany predicate now includes `retryCount > 1` in an OR branch. The pre-PR query used only method and scheduledDate and could be served by the existing `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])`. The new `retryCount > 1` predicate has no supporting index. Because one OR branch is unindexed, this can force a full sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron invocation. WorkflowReminder grows with bookings multiplied by workflow steps, potentially millions of rows, and the cron runs frequently, making this a material query efficiency regression introduced by the diff.

The `retryCount` column added at schema.prisma:1000 has no @@index defined for it, and the migration only adds the column. This leaves the new `retryCount > 1` predicate in deleteMany unsupported by an index.
The migration only adds the `retryCount` column and does not add an index for it, contributing to the unindexed `retryCount > 1` predicate in deleteMany.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.texto: WHAT: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is defined but never called anywhere (grep finds only the definition; `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly). WHY: the intended 'restart only the process that owns a given shard' restart path is unreachable, leaving unused code that suggests the shard-level restart wiring was meant to be used and never got connected. HOW: remove the method, or wire `_ensure_processes_alive` to restart only the affected process if per-shard restart is the goal.

WHAT: the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` (with the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') is neutralized because line 15 monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so it performs no actual wait. WHY: there is no synchronization ensuring the flusher thread observes `current_drift.value = 9000` and flushes before `step.join()` sets `stopped`, so the flusher can exit without producing the expected message, making test_basic flaky. HOW: use an unpatched wait (e.g. `from time import sleep` imported before the monkeypatch, or a real event/poll loop) instead of the patched `time.sleep`.

WHAT: `submit()` now calls `get_memory_info()` on every buffer in `self.buffers`, and each call runs `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` which issues a cluster-wide `INFO` over all nodes (memory.py:82). WHY: since every SpansBuffer returns the identical cluster-wide data, this performs N redundant cluster INFO scans per submit and sums `used`/`available` N times; once `flusher_processes` is scaled toward one-per-shard (the PR's intent) this becomes O(shards) duplicated expensive Redis round trips on a per-batch path. HOW: compute the cluster memory usage once (it is not shard-scoped) instead of aggregating across buffers.

WHAT: `process.kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, but the flusher processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` with `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, which produces a `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` and `multiprocessing.Process` (= `multiprocessing.context.Process`) are sibling subclasses of `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, so the isinstance test is False and `kill()` is never called. WHY: before this PR `self.process.kill()` was unconditional; now an unhealthy/hung flusher process is left alive while `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` immediately starts a new process for the same shard set, so two processes concurrently flush the same Redis shards -> duplicate segments produced to Kafka, and orphaned process accumulation until `process_restarts` exceeds MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS and crashes the consumer. HOW: test against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or the concrete `SpawnProcess` type, or `hasattr(process, 'kill')`) so real spawn processes are killed before restart/terminate.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.texto: The PR removed the function-wide `cacheMu.Lock()` that used to serialize every `BuildIndex` call, keeping only the final cache insert locked here. Two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the SAME key (realistic: two concurrent RPCs both call `getOrCreateIndex`, both observe `GetIndex`==nil, and both build) can now execute `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the identical file-based directory at line 96-98 in parallel, and both write `b.cache[key]`, whereas previously the global lock forced them to run one at a time. Concurrent creation on the same index directory can fail or corrupt the on-disk index, and one of the two built indexes is silently orphaned. Serialize builds per key (or re-check the cache inside a lock before writing) rather than relying on the coarse lock removal.

The newly added `s.search.TotalDocs()` call runs at startup while the watcher goroutine started at line 207 can concurrently invoke `getOrCreateIndex` -> `build` -> `b.cache[key] = idx`. `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` (bleve.go:146) iterates `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`, so a concurrent insert triggers Go's `fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write`. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` inside `TotalDocs` (or snapshot the map under the lock) before calling it here.
